title: The VFX Supervisor Daily
description: What the day's VFX news means, in a few lines, with a link to every story.

items.title: #34: Disguise gets a new owner as US credit hopes and budgets shift
items.summary: Disguise is heading to Yamaha, which may matter if you specify its stages, though nothing changes at closing. The US credit push has a short lame-duck window.
items.content_html:
Disguise is heading to Yamaha, which may matter if you specify its stages, though nothing changes at closing. The US credit push has a short lame-duck window. October's starts skewed smaller, and the next big bids are likely to cluster in February to April.

Yamaha buys Disguise

Press reports put the price at about $283 million, with closing expected in December. Nothing changes for current projects: brand, teams and customers stay as they are, and roadmap news is due in 2027. If you spec Disguise stages, watch whether future joint products stay open to rival gear.

  • Yamaha to acquire Disguise in expansion of visual technology business · newscaststudio.com, also reported by redsharknews.com and techtimes.com Revenue slipped from £67m to £60m and Unreal-based rivals are pressing at the high end, so expect pricing and support to be tested

US federal film credit

The sticking point is finding a legislative vehicle, and one congressman called passage in the lame-duck session 'pretty low'. Do not price a US credit into bids yet.

  • Amid Flight Halt, Trump Meets With Jon Voight to Talk U.S. Film Incentive: ‘Get This Done!’ · variety.com The rebate would cover domestic labour only, and the lame-duck window is short, so treat it as upside rather than a bid assumption
  • Trump Says Federal Film Tax Credit Is Gaining Momentum · hollywoodreporter.com Trump says momentum is building, a sign the push continues, though the headline alone gives no sign of passage

Vendor splits and delivery at scale

Update: Ramayana's scale is now stated: 9,500 shots over a 600-day post schedule, with creature design the weak point in reviews.

  • Wētā FX Goes Out on 29 Limbs to Create 'Resident Evil' VFX · awn.com A practical-first director still needed digital to take over what could not be built, a useful pitch angle for hybrid work
  • Ramayana’s VFX Verdict : Epic Scale Meets Digital Friction · outlookindia.com Delivery at 9,500 shots gets judged in public, and creatures and crowds drew the sharpest criticism, so bid those with care

Dark Slope's Vancouver stage

Update: the Vancouver capacity now has a location and a date. A new Dark Slope stage at North Shore Studios is due to open in December. It gives productions in Vancouver an LED volume option on an eight-stage campus.

  • Dark Slope Announces New Virtual Production Stage at North Shore Studios in Vancouver · auganix.org A December opening gives you a named Vancouver volume to quote, plus a greyboxing lab on site

Production volume and budgets

Only one XL start sits in the next three months, then the calendar fills from February to April, with the UK holding the deepest forward XL pipeline.

  • October Rises 9% as Budgets Skew Smaller · lbbonline.com Expect tight budgets on smaller shows now, and big-show bidding to pick up from February, with the UK a strong market

items.title: #33: Camera-mounted capture and supplier upheaval could change how you bid
items.summary: On-set depth capture is moving closer to the camera, which may change what you quote for matchmove.
items.content_html:
On-set depth capture is moving closer to the camera, which may change what you quote for matchmove. Meanwhile ownership and leadership shifts at studios, suppliers and a UK stage site are worth tracking before you commit to partners or locations.

Update: Mantis puts depth capture on the camera

Update: Hexagon has now launched Mantis, a solid-state LiDAR that records depth frame by frame as the camera rolls. If it works as described, matchmove and set-scan assumptions in your bids may shift. Pricing and real-world results are not given, so treat it as worth watching.

  • Hexagon Mounts a LiDAR on the Cinema Camera Itself to Kill VFX’s Costliest Bottleneck · techtimes.com Claims a per-frame spatial record and Alembic output feeding Unreal, which could trim matchmove cost and LED-stage calibration work if it holds up
  • Hexagon’s New Mantis On-Set 3D Capture System for VFX · postperspective.com Confirms the launch and the standard EXR, FBX and Alembic outputs, so it should slot into existing pipelines without a rebuild

Update: Gedeon Media's assets land with Autentic

Update: Autentic has been confirmed as the winning bidder, and production continues through a new Paris arm, Gedeon Studios, led by Carine Nonnenmacher. This is factual TV, so the VFX impact is small. It suggests distressed European producers are being absorbed rather than closed.

  • Autentic acquires Gedeon Media’s assets and sets up new studio arm · c21media.net A sign that buyers are consolidating failed European producers; if you pitch to such outfits, expect new owners and smaller teams

Studio ownership and space

Ownership changes and facility risk affect who you can partner with and where you can shoot or book space. Check the current owner before you subcontract or tie a bid to a facility.

  • Could Elstree Film Studios be put up for sale? · tvbeurope.com The council says continued investment is not sustainable and alternative uses are on the table, so UK stage availability at Elstree is worth watching
  • CCH hands VFX studio Wanget back to its founder via MBO · app.dealroom.co

Supplier and platform risk

Your pipeline leans on a few big technology suppliers, and both are in flux. Neither changes your bid today, but they are worth watching for pricing, roadmap and AI-workflow shifts.

  • Jensen Huang Out as NVIDIA CEO · Animation World Network
  • Vizrt acquires digital broadcast titling and graphics systems company Chyron · tvbeurope.com Suggests broadcast tooling is consolidating around AI platforms, which may bring new workflow demands if you do live or graphics work

Who did what on current shows

These credits show how vendors are split on current work and which practical-versus-digital choices clients accept. Useful reference when you pitch similar creature or episodic work.

  • Female leadership in VFX for action-crime series Neagley – behind the scenes with WeFX · britishcinematographer.co.uk A Toronto vendor delivered more than 250 shots with about 70 artists in eight months, a useful benchmark for mid-size episodic scope
  • Below: Matt Glover (Production VFX Supervisor) and Annie Godin (Production VFX Producer) · artofvfx.com Shows a lead vendor taking about two thirds of a show, with smaller shops brought in for CG fire and overflow when the schedule tightened
  • How Ludo Studio Made 'Allen': Gecko Smiles, Eight Puppets and an Animatronic That "Didn't Fly" · whats-on-netflix.com A full animatronic failed a test with Netflix and the team switched to puppets, a reminder that practical creature routes can still win
  • Discover how EDI created a photorealistic CG jaguar for Ferine · cgchannel.com A small Italian house built a photorealistic CG creature, useful as a reference for expressive animal work on a modest budget

items.title: #32: Incentive money is moving work between territories while AI settles into post
items.summary: France is paying more for VFX just as UK inward spend falls, and the US federal credit faces political risk.
items.content_html:
France is paying more for VFX just as UK inward spend falls, and the US federal credit faces political risk. For bids, location and rebate maths matter more this quarter. AI is also arriving inside the editing and review tools clients already use, so expect questions about it.

Update: France's rebate gets bigger

Update: France has widened its rebate so non-EU actors' salaries now count as eligible spend, and CNC reports a jump in scouting requests from Hollywood. VFX spend there rose in 2025. Worth pricing France against Italy and Spain on any bid with a large VFX share.

  • How France overhauled investment infrastructure and tax rebate in bid to woo large scale film and TV projects · screendaily.com The 40% rate for local VFX spend over €2m and rising US interest make French vendors or a French split worth pricing

Update: UK inward spend slumps

Update: UK film and TV spend fell sharply in the first three quarters of 2026, with inward investment hit hardest. Co-production is the exception. Expect tougher competition for UK-based work, and consider co-production structures when pitching.

  • Inward film spend in UK down 40% from January-September 2026, but co-production up 31% · screendaily.com

US federal credit: promising but fragile

A federal production credit could pull work back to the US, and stacked with state credits it may reach up to 57%. That would change where US-funded shows choose to shoot and post. The bill's fate depends on politics, so treat it as upside, not a planning assumption.

  • Democrats Won. When Do Hollywood Crews Get Back to Work? · indiewire.com The lame-duck push is the first test, and a political fallout could stall a credit that would shift US-funded work
  • “We need to bring Tom Cruise home,” say cheerleaders of US federal incentive · screendaily.com Up to 57% combined with state credits would be a strong lure for US productions, so worth watching if it advances

AI moves into the tools you already use

AI is arriving inside editing, review and studio workflows rather than as separate apps. Clients may arrive with AI-made placeholders or edits, which affects how you scope and price shots. A studio tying up with a tool maker also hints at where in-house pipelines may head.

  • Adobe Brings AI Agents to After Effects, Premiere at Adobe MAX 2026 · Animation World Network Agent assistants in After Effects and Premiere could change how quickly clients expect comps and revisions, so check your own pipeline
  • Avid’s Ready to Play Brings Google AI Models to Media Composer · postperspective.com Editors can now generate placeholder shots and remove objects like boom mics, which may reshape what lands in your VFX turnover
  • The Last Mile: How Rodeo FX Brought xSTUDIO Into Daily Production · aswf.io A two-engineer team adapting an open source review tool shows a small studio can build custom pipeline tools cheaply
  • Adobe and Disney Announce Multi-Year AI Alliance · Animation World Network Disney's custom models trained on its own properties suggest some studio work may go to in-house AI, so worth watching
  • iQIYI Launches Chinas First AI Film Studio in Shanghai, with Inaugural Title Cop in Trouble in Production · en.antaranews.com A Chinese platform pairing live action with AI post is a possible sign of cheaper rivals, though this is a press release

Credited work and skills funding

Credited shows are useful pricing and positioning references, and public skills money is open to organisations that train people in AI and virtual production. If you plan to go independent, these are routes to credibility and new skills, not direct work.

  • Charting the Visual Effects for 'One Piece' Season 2 · awn.com A 4,058-shot season run with returning vendors shows long-running shows reward vendors who stay close to the supervisor and producer
  • Ferine: EDI Effetti Digitali Italiani Brings a Panther to Life · artofvfx.com A creature-focused making-of from an Italian studio shows what a smaller shop can show off to win creature work
  • NFTS, Falmouth University awarded £650,000 from BFI to support industry use of AI, virtual production · screendaily.com Funded AI and virtual production R&D for UK independents may produce free findings you can use when advising clients
  • Screen Ireland and Northern Ireland Screen open €1.25m Shared Horizons Fund for all-island skills · scannain.com The 1 December deadline and two-partner rule favour organisations, so you would likely need to join a consortium to benefit

items.title: #31: Owner-funded VFX, cheaper stages and AI cost claims all bear on your next bid
items.summary: Virtual production is getting smaller and cheaper, and AI vendors are now putting numbers on savings, which clients may quote back at you.
items.content_html:
Virtual production is getting smaller and cheaper, and AI vendors are now putting numbers on savings, which clients may quote back at you. Big VFX work is also being steered by owners and consolidating parents. Expect pressure on price and on who holds the work.

Update: Manchester gets a 44m stage

Update: a temporary 44m by 5m volume was built at Versa in Manchester with Mars Volume, so large LED capacity can be assembled for a single job. Worth asking whether a pop-up volume suits a one-off shoot before you quote for a fixed stage.

  • Versa installs 44m long VP stage in Manchester · broadcastnow.co.uk A temporary stage of this size, built with a partner for one event, is a model you could price a short volume shoot against

Update: Nuke Stage heads to the Mac

Update: Foundry says Nuke Stage macOS support arrives in early access in 2027, with DMX lighting and output mapping added. Small in-camera VFX setups could get cheaper, which may undercut quotes for smaller volume work.

  • Foundry’s Nuke Stage macOS Support and Education Licensing · content-technology.com Mac-based in-camera VFX would lower the entry cost for small stages and may pull smaller jobs away from big volumes

Update: Ramayana is funded by its VFX owner

Update: Namit Malhotra, DNEG's CEO, says he is funding Ramayana with his own money, and DNEG is in charge of its visual effects. The film also uses AI-assisted lip-synced dubbing from Hindi to English. That suggests owner-backed projects may keep VFX in-house, leaving independents fewer bids.

  • The $500 million gamble to make India’s ‘Ramayana’ a global phenomenon · cnn.com Owner-funded projects with a VFX studio in charge may never reach an open bid, so independents should look for overflow work

AI tools and cost claims reach the pipeline

Vendors now quote cost and time savings, and clients may repeat them when you bid. The more credible tools keep artists in control: editable 3D, preserved source media. Treat Epic's agent-built preview as a test, not a production choice.

  • Animaj Unveils FlipMove AI Animation Workflow · Animation World Network
  • Avid’s Ready to Play brings AI video generation directly into Media Composer · provideocoalition.com Editors can generate temp shots and remove items like a boom mic, which may shift what clients expect to see before final VFX
  • Unreal Engine 5.9 divides game devs with an AI-heavy update · creativebloq.com/3d Epic says parts of the agent-written code are prototypes, so staying on a stable release for live jobs looks prudent
  • CAA and Ogilvy Unveil ECHO AI Celebrity Ad Platform · Animation World Network Ogilvy's new ECHO platform licenses the likeness, voice and IP of CAA clients who opt in and turns a short shoot into many assets, which could squeeze commercial shoot and comp budgets.
  • Virtual Production Finds Its Middle Ground with Blackmagic · content-technology.com Neon Vision puts about 80% of its LED work on 2D backgrounds, a cheaper volume option you could offer small clients

Cuts, new funding rules and credited work

Consolidation is cutting client-side teams, and Italy is rebuilding its incentive system. Credited work shows who wins big shows: studios that join at bidding stage and bring specialist skills.

  • Skydance Games Cuts Staff, Scales Back Projects · Animation World Network Skydance's cuts follow a $6 billion savings target, so expect tougher vendor terms from a consolidating parent
  • Italy establishes a new Cinema and Audiovisual Agency - Institutions / Legislation - Italy · cineuropa.org Italy's tax credit and co-production detail is still to come in implementing decrees, so it is worth watching if you bid for European work
  • JUSTICE PREVAILS FOR DNEG AND COYOTE VS. ACME · vfxvoice.com DNEG used a cell-shaded pipeline and mixed animators with VFX artists to match 2D cartoon characters, a skill set you can pitch
  • Project Hail Mary: Stuart Penn & Bob Winter (VFX Supervisors) and Arslan Elver (Senior Animation Supervisor) – Framestore · artofvfx.com

items.title: #30: Hybrid AI pipelines reach paid VFX work as DC and Netflix buyers shift
items.summary: Framestore's Sky spot puts AI inside a conventional VFX pipeline on a paid job, while cinematographers argue about it publicly.
items.content_html:
Framestore's Sky spot puts AI inside a conventional VFX pipeline on a paid job, while cinematographers argue about it publicly. Meanwhile DC gets a new creative chief and buyers keep consolidating. Worth watching: how clients start asking for AI in bids, and who now signs off at DC.

AI and volumes inside real pipelines

Framestore used AI for previs, environments and character removal, with named supervisors and human control kept in place. That is a template for how clients may expect AI to be priced and credited. The volume piece is a reminder to scope LED work honestly: wide shots can end up as full VFX.

  • Framestore Brings Hybrid AI/VFX to Sky's Christmas Campaign · awn.com Gives you the credit structure and task split of a hybrid AI/VFX job, useful when writing your own AI line items
  • Framestore delivers previs, hybrid AI and animation for Sky’s Christmas campaign · tvbeurope.com Shows AI used for previs, matte painting and character removal alongside traditional comp, a model for pitching controlled AI use
  • Cinematographers’ Favorite Festival Is All About AI This Year, but Artists Still Hate the Tech · indiewire.com Cinematographers voiced bleak views while directors sounded more open, so expect clients on the same job to disagree about AI
  • Standardising the illusion · britishcinematographer.co.uk A working DP says true wide shots in a volume usually become full VFX shots, which affects how you scope and bid
  • Cloud Imperium Games expands VERSA Studios partnership with Squadron 42 showcase and BTS filming · britishcinematographer.co.uk A new large volume in Manchester, built with a specialist partner, is another UK stage option, though this job was event work

DC leadership change

Gunn and Safran leave DC's top jobs and Jeremy Latcham takes over on 1 December, reporting into Skydance. A new head of film, TV and animation could reshape slate priorities and vendor relationships, which may open or close doors. Treat that as interpretation until his first decisions land.

  • DC Studios Shakeup: James Gunn, Peter Safran Stepping Down as Co-CEOs, Marvel Vet Jeremy Latcham Named Chief Creative Officer · indiewire.com Mixed box office and a new creative chief suggest DC's slate and vendor choices could change, so watch early announcements
  • DC Studios Co-Chiefs James Gunn, Peter Safran Step Down · Animation World Network

Update: incentives and where productions go

Update: Ireland is now the clearest example of runaway production chasing incentives, with record spend and stages often full. Canada has also now said how its C$600m funding package will be split. Both affect where your shows shoot and which co-production routes are open.

  • Carney gov’t sets out how Canada’s $425m funding boost will be shared · Canada's federal government has set out how its C$600m (US$425m) relief package for audiovisual and audio industries will be shared, which could ease funding pressure for producers. Money flows mainly through existing Canadian funders, with the CMF running new programmes, so check what reaches production and training

Update: who delivered the work

Update: the Mandalorian issue names the vendor split behind ILM, and the Godzilla piece shows a VFX-led team reusing ride research. Cliff Booth shows a smaller named vendor on a Fincher feature. Useful for sizing competitors and for pitch references.

  • Mando’s miniatures, puppets, stop-motion and more · befores & afters Shows ILM-led work farmed to Image Engine, Hybride, Lola and others, plus Tippett on stop-motion: a map of who gets overflow
  • King Ghidorah Is Ready for Its Close-Up: How ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Cracked the Legendary Monster’s Next Evolution · indiewire.com Creature design reused from a theme-park ride shows prior R&D can become a selling point on later films
  • The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth · artofvfx.com Ollin VFX is credited on a Fincher feature releasing this month, worth tracking as a rival on prestige work

items.title: #29: Public VP stages and co-production deals could change how small studios bid
items.summary: State-funded virtual production space and treaty co-productions are giving small teams routes to big-studio capability.
items.content_html:
State-funded virtual production space and treaty co-productions are giving small teams routes to big-studio capability. Godzilla Minus Zero's opening suggests VFX-led work from outside Hollywood can still draw a global audience. Worth watching: how the Academy treats AI-built animation.

Public virtual production capacity

Korea is putting a large LED stage with 360-degree tracking into public hands for small producers. That could lower the cost of a VP option in a bid. It may also pull some regional work towards state-backed facilities. Worth watching for similar schemes elsewhere.

  • CJ OliveNetworks Wins South Korea's KOCCA Contracts for Daejeon Virtual Production Studio and DMS UHD Post-Production Upgrade, Targeting December Completion · finance.biggo.com A public LED wall of 18.5m by 8m, aimed at small producers, could undercut private VP stage costs in Korean-linked bids
  • When the actor moves, the virtual background follows the actor... CJ OliveNetworks wins K-content production facility project · mk.co.kr The stated aim of cutting costs and timelines, plus UHD/HDR post for OTT delivery specs, shows what public facilities will pitch against independents

Co-production routes for animation

A treaty co-production pairing an Australian animation studio with a new Dublin post and VFX house is a template for splitting work across territories. A planned slate of seven features could mean steady work for partner studios. The job estimate is the studio's own claim.

  • Brisbane’s Like a Photon Creative looks to Ireland for animated feature Familiar · screenhub.com.au Elephant Goldfish's role on a seven-film slate shows a new Irish VFX and post partner for animation work, with finance tied to the treaty

AI-built animation and the Oscars

If an AI-built feature competes with a hand-crafted stop-motion film, the Academy may have to say what counts as animation. The outcome could shape how clients view ML-heavy pipelines and how you describe your own methods in a bid.

  • VFXwire - VFX news: visual effects, film, games & animation · vfxwire.com An awards ruling on an AI-built feature could set the tone for how clients and voters treat ML-assisted work

Godzilla and the value of VFX-led films

Minus Zero's opening follows a predecessor that won the VFX Oscar as a non-English-language film. That suggests a strong VFX reputation can carry a franchise sequel internationally. Creature credits from this team may be worth tracking for future hiring and bidding.

  • ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ roars with $63m at global box office; ‘Ramayana: Rise Of A Legend’ strong with $52.2m; ‘The Cat In The Hat’ leads US openers · screendaily.com A $63m global opening for a Japanese-made sequel to an Oscar-winning VFX film backs the case for VFX-driven work outside the studio system
  • "Two giant kaiju interacting physically": Godzilla Minus Zero director brought retired Japanese animator back for King Ghidorah · soapcentral.com

items.title: #28: AI platforms aim at the full VFX pipeline, so bids may need an AI position
items.summary: An all-in-one AI filmmaking platform is pitching itself at work that independent VFX teams are usually hired for.
items.content_html:
An all-in-one AI filmmaking platform is pitching itself at work that independent VFX teams are usually hired for. Worth deciding now how your bids treat AI, before clients ask.

AI moves into the production pipeline

Tools are being sold as covering story, assets, VFX, editing and grade in one place, with logs of models, prompts and costs. That could shift what clients expect to pay for, and what they ask you to show. Worth having a clear stance on AI use, tracking and human review.

  • AI Filmmaking Platform Core Studio Launches at Taiwan Creative Content Fest With 24 Specialized Agents · variety.com Its VFX, grade and cost-tracking agents target work you might bid on, and the audit trail hints at what clients may want to see
  • Hollywood Has Flipped on GenAI, Says ‘Avatar’ VFX House Weta FX Chief: ‘If You Don’t Have an AI Strategy, Don’t Bother’ · imdb.com Clients will expect a stated AI strategy in bids

items.title: #27: Weta says studios now want a vendor AI plan before they will hire
items.summary: Weta's chief says big clients have moved from banning generative AI to expecting vendors to have a plan for it, which bears directly on how you pitch.
items.content_html:
Weta's chief says big clients have moved from banning generative AI to expecting vendors to have a plan for it, which bears directly on how you pitch. Stage supply and incentive rules are shifting too, and those feed straight into bid budgets.

Update: incentives and market conditions

Update: the new items are about money in the budget. A proposed US federal credit and Hungary's lifted cap could change where shows are priced and shot. Treat both as inputs to scenario bids, not settled facts.

  • “Cautious” buyers head to AFM at critical time for independent sector · screendaily.com A proposed 20% transferable US credit, stackable with state incentives, could pass by early next year, so model it in US-shoot bids
  • Can Hungary rebuild film industry trust in the post-Orban era? · screendaily.com Hungary's cap on its 30% rebate was removed by July, so Budapest is again priceable after producers lost projects

Shows and who did the work

Breakdowns give you scope benchmarks for mid-size vendors and show how small houses win and credit work. Use them for team size, schedule and shot-count comparisons when you scope your own bids.

  • Neagley: WeFX Breaks Down Its Visual Effects Work · artofvfx.com About 70 artists for eight months on 250-plus shots is a usable benchmark for scoping episodic work
  • Roxel Creative Shares 'Backrooms' VFX Breakdown Reel · Animation World Network Roxel's supervisor also held the film's associate VFX supervisor credit, a pattern worth noting when you structure vendor roles
  • Stranger Things live-action prequel series set for Netflix in 2028 · c21media.net A 2028 Netflix prequel is far off and names no vendors, so it is a long-lead item to track

items.title: #26: Italy's reform and studio ownership moves reshape where and with whom to bid
items.summary: Italy has passed its film reform but left the tax credit details for later, so it is a watch item rather than a bidding lever.
items.content_html:
Italy has passed its film reform but left the tax credit details for later, so it is a watch item rather than a bidding lever.

Tax incentives and policy

Italy's reform promises easier permits and co-production rules, but no new credit rates yet. Those depend on decrees due within two years. Worth tracking if you pitch Italian shoots, but do not build a budget on it. Pact's note on UK employment rights is a compliance point for UK-based work.

  • Italy passes sweeping film and TV reform, with measures to attract international shoots · screendaily.com Italy's credit rates are unchanged for now, so treat it as a future option for incoming shoots and not a bid assumption
  • Pact Homepage · pact.co.uk New UK employer duties on union access and harassment are now in effect, which affects any UK company you run or hire through

Update: Weta FX and Taiwan

Update: Weta is investing in Taiwanese house Moonshine Studio and setting up a joint venture to bring local work up to international standard. It is still thin on pricing, so the question is whether Taiwan becomes a credible sub-vendor option.

  • Weta FX Partners With TAICCA To Position Taiwan As AI Hub; Invest In Moonshine Studio · uk.news.yahoo.com A named investment in Moonshine and a joint venture suggest a new Asian vendor option tied to Weta, though rates and capacity are not stated

Studio deals and ownership

Independent studios are finding ways to scale. 1920 VFX stays independently owned after a management buyout, with a Bangalore site opened in 2025. EightyEight Pictures and WildBrain have struck a CG production partnership, which could signal how animation studios share CG capacity, though the details are still worth watching. If you sub work out, expect more partners with India-based production arms.

  • ​1920 VFX completes founder-backed management buyout · shots.net A stable, investor-backed independent London vendor with a Bangalore site is a possible partner or benchmark for your own bids
  • WildBrain, EightyEight Pictures Strike CG Production Partnership · awn.com Shows a client outsourcing CG execution to an India-based vendor while keeping creative control in-house, a model you may be asked to match

Virtual production and new tools

Vancouver LED capacity is being rebuilt after Sony's Pixomondo closure, and Dark Slope is also launching a consulting arm for custom stage builds. That gives you another route to a volume in Canada. Training and tool items show where crew skills and pipelines are heading.

  • Dark Slope to Open New Virtual Production Stage in Vancouver (Exclusive) · hollywoodreporter.com A new Vancouver LED stage from December gives you a volume option in an incentive-rich market, plus a consultancy for custom builds
  • How to get more women working with virtual production in the Nordics? · nordiskfilmogtvfond.com Shows virtual production skills are being actively trained in the Nordics, which may widen the crew pool outside the usual hubs
  • fxguide · fxguide.com Headlines point to generative AI and Nuke plugin developments, worth a look for pipeline planning, though the excerpt gives no detail

Notable shows and who did the work

Vendor splits on recent shows are useful references for how work gets divided. Weta FX led Resident Evil and Moana with smaller specialists alongside, while Silverlake Studios was sole vendor on a 400-shot series.

  • The Pedestrian, Mutant Bryan and all the crazy creatures in Zach Cregger’s ‘Resident Evil’ · befores & afters Resident Evil's 708 shots were split across Weta FX, UPP, Wylie Co. and Lola, a template for a multi-vendor bid
  • fxpodcast: Wētā FX brings the ocean, lava and islands of Moana to life · fxguide Weta FX's 441 shots on Moana show how a lead vendor can take a defined chunk, such as the third act, of a larger show
  • The Drop: A Snowfall Saga – A Look at the VFX Created by Silverlake Studios · artofvfx.com A sole-vendor award of over 400 shots on a streaming series shows mid-size studios can win whole shows

11 links checked when this went out, 0 dead.

items.title: #25: Tax credits are steering post and VFX work, so early planning decides who wins bids
items.summary: Incentives are shaping where post and VFX money lands, from New York to the UK.
items.content_html:
Geoff's take: It's nothing new that tax incentives have a big influence on where film work gets done, but a trend of producers working with VFX earlier in the process is welcomed.

Incentives are shaping where post and VFX money lands, from New York to the UK. Vendors who join projects early and offer several disciplines under one roof look best placed. Worth watching how that shapes the packages you bid into.

Incentives pull post capacity into place

Harbor's bigger New York base follows an extended state tax credit, which suggests incentives still steer where facilities invest. For a Copenhagen bidder, that may mean stronger US competition for multi-discipline post packages, and a reason to check which credits sit under any co-production.

  • Harbor Opens New Flagship Studios in New York, LBB · lbbonline.com A large multi-discipline New York facility, tied by the source to the credit's extension to 2037, may sharpen competition for US-linked post work
  • Harbor Opens Second New York City Post Studio in Hudson Square · postperspective.com Confirms the same opening and room count independently, and the credit link, so the expansion looks like a settled investment rather than a one-off claim

Early VFX involvement and indie co-production funding

The Loc Studios says UK credits are lifting independent features and that early input on recces and shoot planning gave its best results. That is a model worth copying in bids: sell supervision before the shoot. It is one UK studio's view, so treat it as a signal.

  • The Loc Studios expands into on-set VFX · televisual.com Shows a rival pitching early recce and planning input, and co-productions mixing UK, Canadian and Portuguese incentives, which may open doors for Nordic partners

Big shows and who delivered them

Credits and scale figures on tentpoles help benchmark crew size, hours and shot counts when pricing comparable work. They also show which vendors are winning visible sequences, useful when judging competitors and partners.

  • 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day': Sony Pictures Imageworks' Web-Tastic VFX · Animation World Network Gives usable benchmarks: 260 artists, over 101,000 hours and 449 shots, plus the simulation-heavy sequence the team called labour-intensive
  • The Bluff: El Ranchito Showcases Storm and Crocodile VFX · artofvfx.com El Ranchito's storm, ships and crocodile work is a reference for water and creature capability at a vendor you may meet in bids

Post planning at packaging stage

The piece argues producers should bring post in when packaging a project, to cut costs and ease casting. If it holds, it supports pushing for earlier VFX involvement in your own bids.
